Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. | FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place.   PPL PRPs

| 4 | Waste Disposal | PRP for Waste Disposal | The purpose of this PRP is to outline the procedure for managing waste on site to maintain a sanitary/clean environment necessary for the production of products of the highest quality and safety. | 1.0 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has put systems in place to ensure that waste materials are identified, collected, removed and disposed in a manner which prevents contamination of products and production areas.  2.0 Types of Waste The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as; 2.1 Plastic waste-flexible films 2.2 General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen and other office supplies 2.3 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities.    3.0 Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances 3.1 The following standards and guidelines are put in place regarding containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances:  3.1.1 Containers are clearly identified for their various intended purposes;  3.1.2 Located in designated areas;  3.1.3 Constructed of impervious material which can be readily cleaned and sanitized;  3.1.4 Made up of lids which are closed when not in immediate use  3.1.5 Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product.  4.0  Waste management and removal 4.1 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities are channeled into a septic tank. This is regularly recovered and disposed of by a 3rd party liquid waste management contractor.  4.2 Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic and others. The PE, trim waste and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags. Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.  4.3 The organization ensures that waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste it carries.   Bins positioned at production areas and the warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.  4.4 A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to been carted away for disposal.   4.5 A waste management service has been contracted to remove waste from the main waste area as at when due or as deemed necessary. Records of waste removal is kept.  4.6 All labelled materials, products or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.  4.7 Plastic waste containing PE are disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production. Records of all such disposals are kept.  5.0 Drains and drainage 5.1 All drains on site have been designed, constructed and located to prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products.  5.2 Drains have been constructed according to expected flow loads and constructed away from processing lines.  5.3 The direction of flow of drains constructed does not allow a backflow to clean areas.  5.4 There are no drains within the production shop floor and process areas.   6.0 Cleaning Schedule A cleaning schedule is in place for all drains and waste bins. |  | Health Safety & Environment Officer |  |  | FS/PRP 08/CL02.004 – General Cleaning Monitoring Sheets/Waste Bins    FS/PRP 04.01 – Waste Removal Contract for External Consultant. incident, Poly Products has classified Incidents into three main categories. 7.3.1.1 Major Incident: Release of a product, which is likely to have adverse health effects on consumers. This product is already in the market. 7.3.1.2 Serious Incident: Release of a product, which might not have any adverse health effects on consumers but has serious quality defects which is easily noticeable by consumers. This may have adverse effect on the brand image of the product. 7.3.1.3 Minor Incident: This occurs when manufactured products might have quality and/or consumer safety issues but the products have not yet been distributed (still within the company premises). 7.4 Incident Management Committee (IMC) 7.4.1 In order to deal promptly and decisively in any incident situation, Poly Products has set up an incident management committee (IMC).   Scope Statement Guidance - FSMS
||
It is recommended to use terminology like processing, manufacturing, packing; Not be misleading. Not be vague. So instead of “manufacturing of beverages” it shall define what kind of beverages; (without a list of produced products) Define the main activities and not obvious supporting activities like receiving raw materials, cooking batches of raw materials, human resources etc. unless this is essential to clarify what is meant by the term production; Only refer to the processes, products, in detail when essential for food safety Combat potential confusion among customers and end users (consumers) If the term has a specific set of requirements to be met before it can be used, and those requirements are not fully covered by the scope of the FSMS audit, then it can't be used in the scope. | Additional remarks Always describe the audited processes and products / product groups. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. Inside Security Measures 7.2.2.1 Measures are taken within the perimeter including offices and production areas to ensure security is maintained. 7.2.2.2 Access control has been incorporated into door lock systems to give access to only authorized persons to specific areas of the factory. 7.2.2.3 Signs have been posted at areas to clearly communicate restricted access status. The main purpose of these activities is to protect product from intentional contamination. 7.2.2.4 Access to the raw paper storage and printing inks for instance is restricted. | FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. | FS_PRP_09 | PRP for Pest Control | This PRP outlines the methods that is employed to control all potential pests on the premises of the factory. It details out the specific functions of pest control companies in accessing, executing eradication strategies and ensuring no dead pests are left on site. | A programme to be implemented to prevent risks to food safety in the production halls, offices, the canteen and the entire premises including external surroundings used for food packaging production. | 7.1 Introduction 7.1.1 Poly Products recognizes the need to control pests. These include rodents, snakes, flying and crawling insects and other pests. Hence pest control is an integral part of the organization’s activities.  7.1.2 Areas included in the pest control program are the production areas, offices, warehouses, canteen, stores and the general factory site and its immediate surroundings.  7.1.3 This is done on a regular basis to prevent contamination of products and food contact surfaces.  7.1.4 Poly Products shall engage the services of a qualified pest control agency/contractor to undertake the activity of controlling pests on site. In order to ensure a professional job, Poly Products shall ensure the pest control accredited agency is a registered company by law.   7.2 General Factory There shall be regular at least monthly spraying of the factory against mosquitoes, snakes and other crawling and flying insects. Pesticides shall be employed in this exercise.  7.3 Production Hall 7.3.1 Specific areas in the production hall shall be identified. These areas shall have traps to control rodents.  7.3.2 Insectocutors (special electrical equipment for killing flying insects) shall be installed for the control of insects and flies.  7.4 Offices Periodic disinfection and spraying of insecticides shall be done in offices as per the pest control schedule. All offices shall also have pest traps to control rodents where applicable.   7.5 Warehouses/Stores 7.5.1 All warehouses and stores for raw materials, packaging materials and finished goods shall be fitted with pest traps to control the activities of rodents.  7.5.2 These traps as well as those in other areas on the pest map shall be inspected on a weekly basis except weekends, holidays.  7.5.3 The purpose of this inspection is to pick up any dead rodents for disposal and subsequent replacement of baits, glue-boards as applicable.   7.6 Canteen 7.6.1 The presence of food residue and transient garbage makes the canteen susceptible to pest invasion, especially houseflies, cockroaches and rodents.   7.6.2 Rodent traps shall be placed at possible entry points in the canteen to control rodents. Insectocutors would be installed in the canteen to control houseflies.  7.6.3 Aerosols shall not be permitted in the canteen in order to avoid contamination of food.  7.6.4 The canteen shall be included in the periodic fumigation activity in order to control mosquitoes and cockroaches. All utensils and kitchen equipment including food contact surfaces shall be covered during the fumigation activity. After fumigation, utensils, equipment and food contact surfaces shall be washed and disinfected.  7.7 Approved Chemicals 7.7.1 The pest control contractor shall be asked to present all chemicals to be used for controlling pests on site together with the MSDS.  7.7.2 This shall include chemicals used to control mosquitoes, snakes, mice, rats and other rodents. It is the responsibility of the Food Safety Team Leader to clear all chemicals before application.  7.7.3 As a general rule, canteen and food packaging areas like production areas shall be covered before fumigation exercise irrespective of what chemical it is.  7.7.4 Surfaces and equipment shall be cleaned and disinfected in such peculiar cases.  7.7.5 Physical traps shall include the use of secured bait traps and/or adhesives. The traps and or adhesives shall be placed at each of the bait stations identified.   7.7.6 Pest control agents, cleaners shall inspect the traps on a weekly basis whether any rodent or any other pest has been caught. If there is a rodent trapped, the pest would be picked up and disposed correctly. If it was the cleaner that sighted the pest, the pest control agents will be notified.  7.7.7 If there are no rodents, the personnel checks whether the secured bait is still there or not and if not a new bait is replaced  7.7.8 The Pest Control Agent shall submit monthly reports indicating all activities on site.  7.7.9 The report shall include the type of pesticides used, quantity, concentration used, where, when and how applied, target pests, number of pest traps replaced (if any).  7.8 Trigger Levels 7.8.1 The following activity below will serve as a trigger for the immediate intervention of an external pest controller. The threshold level that will necessitate a trigger are 7.8.1.1 An increase in pest activity in a particular area, or as observed in the pest trend activity report or a sighting of a snake should trigger the intervention of an external pest controller 7.8.1.2 a sighting of a live rat, lizard or reptile within the production hall 7.8.1.3 a sighting of a snake anywhere within the premises 7.8.1.4 any unusual pest activity sighted anywhere on site 7.8.1.5 a spike in pest control trends    7.9 Corrective and Preventative Actions 7.9.1 In the event of a spike in pest trend activity or any of the activity that can trigger as listed in 7.8 above, there should be a documented steps or corrective actions to be taking using the following format as below | Daily, weekly or monthly | Pest Controller, SHE Officer, Food Safety Team Leader | FS/PRP 09/REC 01 Pest Control Report. | FS_PRP_05 | Equipment Suitability, Cleaning & Maintenance | PRP for Equipement Suitabilty, Cleaning & Maintenance | The purpose of this PRP is to ensure that equipment used in production and packaging areas are designed to prevent contamination | 1.0 General Requirements 1.1 Poly Products Company Limited has provided equipment designed to prevent contamination for use in production of food packaging.  2.0  Hygiene Design and food contact surfaces 2.1 Poly Products Company Limited has taken into consideration the potential sources of contamination from equipment constructed with unsuitable material. 2.2 Therefore, all processing equipment are constructed from stainless steel and firm non-leaking and non-wearable plastic material. The construction materials compatible with the intended food packaging, lubricants and cleaning or flushing agents. 2.3 The food contact surfaces of the processing equipment are smooth, accessible and cleanable.  2.4  Equipment components containing metals of known toxicity (e.g. mercury) are excluded from use for the processing of food packaging.  3.0 Maintenance of Equipment  3.1 Poly Products Company Limited has in place a system of planned maintenance which covers all equipment.  3.2 Equipment maintenance programmes are available and systematically applied to minimize the potential for contamination of product by equipment.  3.3 A procedure has been established to remove any potential contaminant from machinery and equipment after maintenance work. Equipment with product contact surfaces after maintenance are released in accordance to line release protocols before being used by production.    3.4 Maintenance personnel are required to follow the prescribed procedures including, where appropriate, hygiene measures. Temporary engineering and modifications are avoided but strictly controlled when they are carried out. | Daily | Maintenance Engineer Food Safety Team Leader Factory Manager | FS/PRP05.01 – Equipment Calibration Schedule    FS/PRP 05.03 – Equipment Cleaning Record    FS_PRP_05 ATTACH 01 – Preventive Maintenance Plan    FS/PRP 01/CL 01 -Facility Inspection Checklist/Report    FS/PRP04.02 – Job Ticket    FS/PRP06/ATTACH01 – Stock Card | Dust and soil particles from environment. | Chemical contamination from lubricants, fuels and detergents. | Microbial contamination from personnel. | GMP protocols for personnel, cleaning and maintenance of equipment, pest control program, use of food grade lubricants and detergents. |

| 4 | Waste Disposal | PRP for Waste Disposal | The purpose of this PRP is to outline the procedure for managing waste on site to maintain a sanitary/clean environment necessary for the production of products of the highest quality and safety. | 1.0 General requirements Poly Products Ltd has put systems in place to ensure that waste materials are identified, collected, removed and disposed in a manner which prevents contamination of products and production areas.  2.0 Types of Waste The types of waste generated at Poly Products Ltd are categorized as; 2.1 Plastic waste-flexible films 2.2 General waste including packages of consumables, food debris from canteen and other office supplies 2.3 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities.    3.0 Containers for waste, inedible or hazardous substances 3.1 The following standards and guidelines are put in place regarding containers for waste and inedible or hazardous substances:  3.1.1 Containers are clearly identified for their various intended purposes;  3.1.2 Located in designated areas;  3.1.3 Constructed of impervious material which can be readily cleaned and sanitized;  3.1.4 Made up of lids which are closed when not in immediate use  3.1.5 Segregated in a demarcated area where the waste may pose a risk to the product.  4.0  Waste management and removal 4.1 Liquid waste from toilet facilities and the main amenities are channeled into a septic tank. This is regularly recovered and disposed of by a 3rd party liquid waste management contractor.  4.2 Solid waste is segregated on a daily basis into general waste, PE waste for recycling, flexible waste for disfiguration and destruction, trim waste, plastic and others. The PE, trim waste and flexible film waste are disposed in plastic bags. Special bins that are durable to hold the various kinds of waste identified are positioned at areas where waste is generated.  4.3 The organization ensures that waste is not allowed to accumulate in product-handling or storage areas. All bins across the site are clearly labelled with the type of waste it carries.   Bins positioned at production areas and the warehouses are removed at least once per shift or when they are full, whichever comes first.  4.4 A dedicated area at the back of the factory premises has been allocated where all empty drums used in the factory are stored prior to been carted away for disposal.   4.5 A waste management service has been contracted to remove waste from the main waste area as at when due or as deemed necessary. Records of waste removal is kept.  4.6 All labelled materials, products or printed packaging materials are disfigured by cutting into shreds before disposal to ensure they cannot be reused or enter the supply chain again.  4.7 Plastic waste containing PE are disposed to a contractor for recycling. Recycled plastic materials are not used on site at any stage of production. Records of all such disposals are kept.  5.0 Drains and drainage 5.1 All drains on site have been designed, constructed and located to prevent the risk of contamination of materials and products.  5.2 Drains have been constructed according to expected flow loads and constructed away from processing lines.  5.3 The direction of flow of drains constructed does not allow a backflow to clean areas.  5.4 There are no drains within the production shop floor and process areas.   6.0 Cleaning Schedule A cleaning schedule is in place for all drains and waste bins. |  | Health Safety & Environment Officer |  |  | FS/PRP 08/CL02.004 – General Cleaning Monitoring Sheets/Waste Bins    FS/PRP 04.01 – Waste Removal Contract for External Consultant. Drain Cleaning Checklist |  |  | Microbial contamination from pests. | Waste containers must be dedicated, secured and covered. Surroundings of waste containers must be kept clean to control pests. Food packaging handlers are exempt from waste disposal. |

|  |  |  |  | 1.1  Microbiological cross-contamination 1.1.1 Poly Products Ltd has identified areas where potential microbiological cross-contamination exists. All these areas were considered during the HACCP study.  1.1.2 To control the likelihood of these hazards occurring, some control measures have been taking as a minimum.   1.1.2.1 The Quality Manager together with the Food Safety Team shall ensure to;  1.1.2.2 Separate non-food items from finished products.  1.1.2.3 Separate areas for the storage of raw materials and finished products. 1.1.2.4 Control access to process areas, the laboratory and any other area identified as medium risk. Only authorized staff are allowed to access such areas of production.  1.1.2.5 Streamline traffic patterns.  1.2 Allergen management 1.2.1 There are no allergens in the food packaging process. Poly Products Ltd has however put in place rigorous cleaning protocols to ensure there are no allergen cross-contact by cleaning agents.  1.2.2 All employees including maintenance staff involved in cleaning of equipment are trained in allergen awareness and associated manufacturing practices.  1.3 Physical contamination 1.3.1 Periodic inspections are done to ensure coverings of machines made of brittle materials such as machine covering made of Perspex and glass components of equipment are intact.   1.3.2 Regular monthly glass audits are carried out and measures put in place to prevent, control or detect potential contamination and corrective actions put in place.  1.3.3 The use of snap off knife blade is forbidden.  1.3.4 Tools are to be locked up in their respective tool boxes and must not be left loose in any place or on surfaces where product contamination can occur  1.4 Chemical contamination 1.4.1  Eliminate or prevent chemical contamination by ensuring that;  1.4.1.1 All lubricants employed in production are food grade.  1.4.1.2 Precautions are taken to ensure that lubricants do not enter into the product.  1.4.1.3 All lubricants are stored in a dedicated area far from the production hall to prevent accidental leakage into products. |  | Food Safety Team Leader, Quality Manager, Food Safety Team |  |  | FS/PRP 08/ATTACH 01 – Master Cleaning Plan     FS/PRP 05.02 – Filter Replacement Record     FS/PRP 07/REC 01 - Monthly Glass/Illumination Inspection Records     MSDS for all chemicals     IMS/WP 01.24/ATTACH 01 – Allergen Declaration GMP Protocols |  | Microbial contamination from personnel and pest. Chemical contamination cleaning chemicals. Physical contamination from dust and soil in the environment. | Medical examination for food handlers and GMP protocols for personnel. Pest control program. | 1 | Establishment | PRP FOR ESTABLISHMENT | The purpose of programme is to outline the construction and layout of the building within which production takes place and how management will maintain the structure to support hygienic manufacture of products. | 1.1 Poly Products Company Limited has provided buildings to support its manufacturing activities.  1.2 The buildings have been designed, constructed and maintained in a manner appropriate to the nature of the processing operations being carried out, the food safety hazards associated with our operations and the potential sources of contamination from the plant environs.  1.3 The buildings are of durable construction which presents no food safety hazard to the product. They are constructed with concrete, aluminim and steel.  2.0  Environment 2.1 Poly Products Company Limited has taken into consideration the potential sources of contamination from the local environment.  2.2 The main source of contamination is dust. The structure and layout of the factory has been designed to prevent the ingress of dust, soil and animals.  2.3 The organization has ensured that the production process takes place in well managed areas to prevent harmful substances from entering the product.  2.4 All measures taken to protect the product against potential contaminants are periodically reviewed to ensure effectiveness.   3.0 Locations of establishments 3.1 Poly Products Company Limited has clearly identified the boundaries of its site, and access to the site is controlled.  3.2 Measures have been put in place to ensure the site is maintained in good order at all times. This include the tendering of vegetation.  3.3 Roads, yards and parking areas have been constructed to drain to prevent standing water when it rains or when washed. These facilities are maintained in an ongoing basis.  3.4 A maintenance programme is in place to ensure that walls, floors, roof, rooms and any other structure on site is fit for purpose. The routine inspection is done annually. |  | Maintenance Manager | Corrective action procedure |  | FS/PRP 02.01 – Building Layout     FS/PRP 01/CL 01 - Monthly Facility Inspection Checklist/Report    FS/PRP 01/ATTACH 01 Improvement Plan for Facility Inspection Report | Dust from envirnmomet, soil from outside, debris, cobweb buildup. | Lubricant, fuel, cleaning, detergent, water | Insects, birds, mice, rats, | Closing or sealing of openings. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place. The idea is to respond quickly to a product contamination threat or event using planned measures. 7.2.4.2 There is already an existing incident management plan which deals with product recalls whether it is food safety related or quality related. 7.2.4.3 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for incident response security; 7.2.4.3.1 Investigating Security Concerns 7.2.4.3.1.1 The incident management procedure specifies how non-conforming products are quarantined. This is the same procedure used to hold potentially harmful products. 7.2.4.3.1.2 The organization encourages reporting of customer complaints and suspicious activities. All these are promptly investigated. 7.2.4.3.1.3 Employees are trained to report any activity that is outside the ways of work and breaches normal factory procedures. A product recall plan is maintained and periodically reviewed and key personnel are trained in product recall procedures. 7.3 Emergency Contact Security 7.3.1 The Human Resource department ensures that employee contact information is kept up to date. 7.3.2 The emergency contact list is also kept up to date by the Emergency Team Leader. | Annual reviw of VACPP and TACCP risk analysis | Food Safety team | VACCP and TACCP Studies | | | | VACCP and TACCP risk analysis and control Measures |

They are constructed with concrete, aluminim and steel.  2.0  Environment 2.1 Poly Products Company Limited has taken into consideration the potential sources of contamination from the local environment.  2.2 The main source of contamination is dust. The structure and layout of the factory has been designed to prevent the ingress of dust, soil and animals.  2.3 The organization has ensured that the production process takes place in well managed areas to prevent harmful substances from entering the product.  2.4 All measures taken to protect the product against potential contaminants are periodically reviewed to ensure effectiveness.   3.0 Locations of establishments 3.1 Poly Products Company Limited has clearly identified the boundaries of its site, and access to the site is controlled.  3.2 Measures have been put in place to ensure the site is maintained in good order at all times. This include the tendering of vegetation.  3.3 Roads, yards and parking areas have been constructed to drain to prevent standing water when it rains or when washed. These facilities are maintained in an ongoing basis.  3.4 A maintenance programme is in place to ensure that walls, floors, roof, rooms and any other structure on site is fit for purpose. site plans and processing details are controlled. 7.2.3 Personnel Security Measures 7.2.3.1 Personnel security is taken seriously. Measures have been put in place to ensure that only authorized personnel are on the factory premises at any point in time. This includes visitors on site. 7.2.3.2 This establishment has in place at least one of the following measures for personnel security; 7.2.3.2.1 Employee Security 7.2.3.2.1.1 During hiring of employees, thorough background checks are done. 7.2.3.2.1.2 Employees are trained to know what they can do on site. 7.2.3.2.1.3 Areas restricted to be accessed by only a category of employees is made known to every employee hired. 7.2.3.2.1.4 Confidentiality clauses are inserted into employment letters. Employees are made to sign the confidentiality agreement. 7.2.3.2.2 Non-employee Security 7.2.3.2.2.1 Provision has been made for non-employees such as visitors, guests, customers, contractors, suppliers, third party drivers etc. 7.2.3.2.2.2 A log of non-employees entering the establishment is maintained at the main security area. 7.2.3.2.2.3 A visitor’s ID card has been designed with numbers and these are assigned to every visitor who enters the facility to conduct one business or the other. 7.2.3.2.2.4 All visitors are mandated to wear their visitor ID cards where they would be very visible. 7.2.3.2.2.5 Non-employees are chaperoned on-site by security or the person they came to transact business with and they are basically restricted to designated areas of the factory. 7.2.3.2.2.6 Non-employees have restrictions on what they can do on site. For instance, non-employees are not permitted to take pictures on site. 7.2.3.2.3 Security Training 7.2.3.2.3.1 All new employees undergo security awareness training. Existing employees undergo periodic security awareness training. 7.2.3.2.3.2 Employees are trained on access control, handling of sensitive information, what suspicious activities look like and reporting such activities to management or the security team. 7.2.4 Incident Response Security Measures. 7.2.4.1 An incident response security references the incident management plan already in place.   Scope Statement Guidance - FSMS
||
|  | The specific sectors (e.g. plastics, paper and board, metal, glass) of packaging manufacture must be taken up in the scope on the certificate. It must also be clear that the manufactured packaging material is intended for the food industry. | FS_PRP_06 | Management of Purchased materials and services | This PRP describes the selection of suppliers for the supply of the types of raw and packaging materials purchased for production and how they are received and stored in the factory. | Procurement of materials and services for use in production must be managed in order to control food safety risks to food packing. | 1.0 Selection and management of suppliers 1.1.1 To ensure the right supplier is selected a hazard assessment, including the potential risk to the final product is used to justify the decision to engage a particular supplier.  1.1.2 The following is done; 1.1.2.1 Assess the supplier’s ability to meet quality and food safety expectations, requirements and specifications.  1.1.2.2 Some of the procedures used for assessing suppliers include; 1.1.2.2.1 Audit of the supplying site prior to accepting materials for production or the provision of relevant certifications or desktop audit.  1.1.2.2.2 Appropriate third-party certification.  1.1.2.2.3 Performance monitoring of the supplier to assure continued approval status. 1.1.2.2.4 Suppliers will be contacted on their performance and be required to reply especially to non-conformances that involves product quality  1.2 Incoming material requirements (raw/ingredients/packaging) 1.2.1 All delivery vehicles are checked prior to, and during, offloading to verify that the quality and safety of the material has been maintained during transit.  1.2.2 All delivered materials are tested and or covered by COA to verify conformity with specified requirements prior to acceptance or use. The method of verification is documented for each item delivered by suppliers.  1.3.3 The inspection frequency is based on the hazard presented by the material and the risk assessment of the specific suppliers.  1.3.4 All non-conforming products are placed on-hold and rejected to be returned back to the supplier. 1.3.5 In cases where purchased items are imported, the supplier is notified of the non-conformance after which the material is either sold to recycling plants in the case of packaging or destroyed under supervision in the case of other items which cannot be recycled. 1.3.6 Criteria for disqualification: 1.3.6.1 Lack of prompt response to complaint or problem identify by the suppliers. 1.3.6.2 Lack of supply of quality raw material in two successions without corrective actions.  1.3.7 All items purchased are stored in demarcated storage areas and released to production for use. | Daily, monthly and anually | Factory Manager, Warehouse Manager, | FS/PRP 06/REC 05 - Approved Suppliers and Service Providers' List  Material Intake Checklist                  FS/PRP 06/FORM 01 – Supplier Monitoring/Tracking sheet     FS/PRP 06/FORM 02 -  Suppliers/Questionnaire Evaluation Form Internal Audit Reports |  | Chemical contamination |  | Procedure for handling and storing food and non-food materials. |

| FS_PRP_11 | PRP for Rework | This PRP details the actions to be taken once it is established, or suspected, that product does not meet the required standards for distribution and hence sale of a product. | Deliberate action must be taken to ensure that non-conforming food packaging meet all established food safety standards prior to release. | 7.1  General Requirements Rework is stored, handled and used in such a way that product safety, quality, traceability and regulatory compliance are maintained.  7.2 Rework can be of three main types: 7.2.1 Out of specification product 7.2.2 In specification product that needs to be re-packed 7.2.3 Product/Trade returns  7.3  Out of Specification Product 7.3.1 This is typically products that has issues with product safety or quality. This could happen to intermediate or finished goods that analysis shows that one or more critical parameters are off. Such parameters may include out of specification of critical quality parameters.  7.3.2 In the case of quality parameters or suspected microbiological contamination, the product is taken through a segregation process to sort out the compliant material from those that cannot be used for production.  The non-conforming material that cannot be re-worked is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4 In Specification Product 7.4.1 Rework can also be generated with products that are within specification but the following may put the product into a rework category. i. Ink-stained finished food packaging ii. issues with the secondary packaging that does not affect the quality and safety of the finished primary food packaging inside. iii. illegible packaging print iv. Poor printing of images and text on finished packaging after a huge quantity has been produced and packed.  7.4.2 In the instance where there are flashes, illegible printing and poor printing of images and text, move all the affected boxes of products to the rework area.  7.4.3 The rework operator shall observe full hygiene rules in the rework area.   7.4.4 The rework operator will then sort the packaging that conforms to standards from the non-conforming products.  7.4.5 The products that conform are then repacked for final inspection by Quality Control whilst the non-conforming products is affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.4.6 Quality Control then releases the conforming products   7.4.7 Rework of finished primary packaging is high risk from a hygiene perspective and must be handled to an agreed strict hygiene protocol.   7.5 Product Returns  7.5.1 Product returns can fall into two main categories 7.5.1.1 Clean trade returns 7.5.1.2 Dirty trade returns such as accident goods and in some cases badly managed packaging.  7.5.2 On arrival of trade returns, QC does a detailed inspection and classifies the returns into clean trade returns and dirty trade returns.  7.5.3 Products that are clean and not damaged are repacked into new secondary packaging under strict hygienic standards.   7.5.4 Secondary packaging are labelled to reflect the manufacturing dates and stocked at the Finished Goods warehouse for dispatch to customers.  7.5.5 Those products with defaced images and text would be affixed with a Reject label and scrapped by cutting into shreds so as to disfigure the materials before been disposed of.  7.5.6 Records of rework shall be kept and all batches with reworked packaging incorporated shall be noted for tracking purposes. | Daily | Rework Operator, Factory Manager, Quality Manager | Rework records, Disposal records. | Jewelry, hair pieces, dust and soil particles. | Chemical contamination from equipment. | Microbial contaminats. Eg. Staphylococcus, E. coli, Salmonella. from personnel. | Medical examination for food handlers and GMP protocols for personnel.  Cleaning and sanitizing program. |

| FS_PRP_05 | Equipment Suitability, Cleaning & Maintenance | PRP for Equipement Suitabilty, Cleaning & Maintenance | The purpose of this PRP is to ensure that equipment used in production and packaging areas are designed to prevent contamination | 1.0 General Requirements 1.1 Poly Products Company Limited has provided equipment designed to prevent contamination for use in production of food packaging.  2.0  Hygiene Design and food contact surfaces 2.1 Poly Products Company Limited has taken into consideration the potential sources of contamination from equipment constructed with unsuitable material. 2.2 Therefore, all processing equipment are constructed from stainless steel and firm non-leaking and non-wearable plastic material. The construction materials compatible with the intended food packaging, lubricants and cleaning or flushing agents. 2.3 The food contact surfaces of the processing equipment are smooth, accessible and cleanable.  2.4  Equipment components containing metals of known toxicity (e.g. mercury) are excluded from use for the processing of food packaging.  3.0 Maintenance of Equipment  3.1 Poly Products Company Limited has in place a system of planned maintenance which covers all equipment.  3.2 Equipment maintenance programmes are available and systematically applied to minimize the potential for contamination of product by equipment.  3.3 A procedure has been established to remove any potential contaminant from machinery and equipment after maintenance work. Equipment with product contact surfaces after maintenance are released in accordance to line release protocols before being used by production.    3.4 Maintenance personnel are required to follow the prescribed procedures including, where appropriate, hygiene measures. Temporary engineering and modifications are avoided but strictly controlled when they are carried out. | Daily | Maintenance Engineer Food Safety Team Leader Factory Manager | FS/PRP05.01 – Equipment Calibration Schedule    FS/PRP 05.03 – Equipment Cleaning Record    FS_PRP_05 ATTACH 01 – Preventive Maintenance Plan    FS/PRP 01/CL 01 -Facility Inspection Checklist/Report    FS/PRP04.02 – Job Ticket    FS/PRP06/ATTACH01 – Stock Card | Dust and soil particles from environment. | Chemical contamination from lubricants, fuels and detergents. | Microbial contamination from personnel. | GMP protocols for personnel, cleaning and maintenance of equipment, pest control program, use of food grade lubricants and detergents. |
